Any Quadri

GeometryConstructions
Game: This is a picture, not a game: three lines drawn across a four-sided shape always meet at one dot.
How to play: Drag the corners A, B, C and D, or focus a corner and use the arrow keys. Tick Hint to see the parallelogram that makes the lines meet.
Look for the math

Drag a corner and the whole shape changes, yet three lines keep passing through the same dot, and that dot is the middle of each one. Here is why that cannot fail.

The three lines

Call the midpoints of the sides AB, BC, CD, DA by K, L, M and N, and the midpoints of the diagonals AC and BD by F and E. The lines KM and LN join midpoints of opposite sides, and EF joins the midpoints of the diagonals; this last line is Newton's line. They all pass through one point G = (A + B + C + D) / 4. Watch the green dot: it sits exactly halfway along each of the three lines, no matter how you drag.

Why they share a middle

In triangle ABD, the segment from E (middle of BD) to N (middle of DA) is parallel to AB and half its length. In triangle ABC, the segment from F (middle of AC) to L (middle of BC) is also parallel to AB and half its length. So EN and LF are equal and parallel, which makes ENFL a parallelogram. Its diagonals EF and NL therefore cut each other in half. The same argument with triangles ADC and BCD makes EKFM a parallelogram, so EF and KM cut each other in half as well. EF has only one middle, so all three lines share it: they are concurrent and each is divided in the ratio 1:1.

The centre of gravity

Put four equal weights at the corners. Combine them two at a time and you get three pairs, whose balance points are exactly those six side and diagonal midpoints. Combining each pair of balance points gives the same barycenter G: the centre of gravity of the four weights. The three bimedians are just the three ways of getting there, which is why they meet.

True for every quadrilateral

The page claims this for any quadrilateral, and the logic test confirms it: on a square, a rectangle, a tilted shape, a dart, a crossed shape and three thousand random quadrilaterals, all three segments have the same midpoint and the error stays around 1e-9 times the size of the drawing. No symmetry or circle is needed: the whole statement is a fact about averages, so it holds even for a crossed or non-convex four-sided shape.

Tick Hint and drag one corner far away: the yellow parallelogram stays a parallelogram, and the dot stays at the middle of every line.
